newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A shares end up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares end up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share market closed up on Monday on a technical rebound supported by bargain-hunting from retail investors after Beijing's ban on state bank funds entering the country's stock markets drove share prices sharply lower last Friday, brokers said.
The A share index rose 5.44 points or 1.24 percent to end at 445.65 on turnover of 7.2 billion yuan against Friday's 12.7 billion yuan.
There was no trading on Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market on Monday due to a public holiday in Hong Kong, the Dragon Boat Festival. Trading will resume on Tuesday.
On Friday, the B share index closed at 150.77, down 6.00 points or 3.83 percent from the previous session, on turnover of HK$87 million.
"Today's rebound was spurred by small investors who anticipated quick profits," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Despite the rally, the market's outlook remains gloomy as banks, which used to be the major institutional investors, pull out of the market, analysts said.

Beijing on Thursday ordered state banks to begin unwinding their equity positions on Friday within 10 sessions, to sqeeze the so called "speculative bubble" out of the stock market. They must also stop trading in treasury debt repurchase agreements.
"The ban has drained some of the market's liquidity and I expect turnover to dwindle this week as investors take a wait-and-see attitude," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The ban will effectively cut off the main source of "hot money" (speculative funds) from the markets, brokers said.
In May, Beijing also banned state and listed enterprises from speculative stock trading, official media have said.
"The B share market will continue to move in tandem with the A share market, but cheaper B share prices should prevent any heavy selling in that market," the Guotai analyst said.
Shanxi Zhangze Electric Power Co Ltd, which debuted in Shenzhen with a flotation of 40 million A shares, closed at 16.98 yuan against an issue price of 6.00 yuan per share.
